args.prompt:
One continuous 30-second take: a single unbroken camera move, no cuts, no jump cuts, no scene changes, no time skips. Smooth gimbal, no shake. 35mm film look, soft natural grain, shallow depth of field.
CAST: @Image1 shows the exact product: a short wide matte ivory stoneware candle with hand-thrown rings, creamy wax, one wooden wick, the word SOL debossed small on the front. It is the only product and the only readable text. It never moves, changes shape or changes size. Its label stays sharp and unchanged.
FIRST FRAME: a cold grey winter morning by a tall window; the unlit candle stands on a dark wooden table beside folded linen and a small stack of books; rain-streaked glass, blue-grey light.
RULES: real physics; one room, one camera path; the light changes continuously like a slow time-lapse of the room warming, never a cut.
[0-6 s] The camera is already drifting slowly forward toward the candle at a calm walking pace; cold blue light, faint rain on the glass.
[6-12 s] A small flame appears on the wick on its own and steadies; a thin warm glow spreads across the wax and the linen.
[12-20 s] Without cutting, the camera arcs gently to the left around the candle at constant speed; the window light shifts from cold blue to soft gold as if the season turns; the rain on the glass fades and dries.
[20-26 s] Warm late-afternoon sunlight pours through the window panes, leaf shadows drift across the wall; the flame flickers softly.
[26-30 s] The camera slows smoothly and settles exactly on the final composition: the lit candle by the golden window, warm and still.
AUDIO: none.
No people, no hands, no text overlays, no extra candles, no logos besides SOL.
